docs.title: The LED
docs.text: Pattern State three short flashes, a pause normal operation: calibrated, no error fast flashing, about ten times a second calibration running a few flashes, then blinking for about 2 s after power-up the bootloader waits for a host before it starts the firmware; it keeps blinking when there is no valid firmware on, steady error mode, or not calibrated off no power, or #LED 0 Normal operation Calibration Error mode

docs.title: The error flags
docs.text:
The flags as the firmware keeps them, the line #Error prints for each, and where each sits in the two bytes of Send_Respond_State_of_Errors (bits numbered from the most significant).

Flag #Error prints Byte, bit Raised when Error In error state! 0, 7 any of the flags below is set (also the error bit of every CAN identifier) temperature_error Temp error 0, 6 the thermistor reads above #Tlim or below −20 °C (with #Term 1) encoder_error Encoder error 0, 5 the encoder reports no magnet (too weak a field) Vbus_error Vbus error 0, 4 the supply is below 9 V or above #Vmax (29000 mV after #Default); from firmware 109 a low supply is not checked in the first 500 ms after power-up Driver_error Driver error (undervoltage, thermal shutdown, or overcurrent) 0, 3 never in this firmware; reserved (STEPFOC reads no fault output of its driver stage) Velocity_error Velocity error 0, 2 the speed exceeds 30,000,000 ticks/s, a fixed threshold (Velocity_limit_error), not #Vlimit Current_error Current error 0, 1 never in this firmware; reserved ESTOP_error Received ESTOP command 0, 0 Send_ESTOP was received Calibrated (0) Not calibrated 1, 7 (1 = calibrated) the motor has not been calibrated Activated — 1, 6 the activated flag, not an error Watchdog_error Watchdog error 1, 5 the watchdog time passed without a motion frame or an answered request wrong_product Wrong firmware for this board (product lock) 1, 4 from firmware 109: the firmware found the other product's stamp, or a calibration its product cannot make, at start-up; it drives nothing

Gripper mode has its own flags in Respond_Gripper_data_pack: a temperature error (a copy of the thermistor error), a timeout error (a copy of the CAN watchdog error, not a move timeout) and an E-stop error, which stays while the E-stop bit is 1; see the Gripper reference.

docs.title: Clearing
docs.text: #Clear and Send_Clear_Error clear every flag except Calibrated and go to idle; a flag whose cause persists is set again at once. The watchdog, E-stop and velocity errors clear and stay clear; the Vbus, encoder and temperature errors come back until the cause is gone, and so does a gripper E-stop while its E-stop bit is 1. Calibration clears the calibration error. A wrong product stays until the right firmware is flashed. Clearing a watchdog error also ends a watchdog hold or descend.

The calls for the messages added in firmware 109 (Send_Parameter, Send_Get_Parameter, Send_Respond_Identity, Send_Respond_Telemetry, Send_Buffer_Read, Send_Cogging_Harmonic, Send_Cogging_Table, Send_Sound, Send_Samples), and the actions 'Coast' and 'Descend' of Send_Watchdog, come with library 1.21. It also adds calls built on the parameters, among them Send_Watchdog_Fallback, Send_Tool_ID, Send_Cogging_Mode, Send_Capture_Setup, Send_Capture_Trigger, Send_Histogram, Send_Cogging_Calibrate and Send_Encoder_Calibrate; the sound calls Send_Tone, Send_Sound_Stop, Send_Sound_Event, Send_Sound_Play, Send_Sound_Clear, Send_Samples_Play and Send_Samples_Stop on top of Send_Sound and Send_Samples; and the module Spectral_BLDC.music (note names, ringtone melodies, MIDI and WAV files as queue events and samples, see Sound).

The same release adds Spectral_BLDC.helpers, blocking functions that send a request and wait for the answer: get_parameter and set_parameter (which reads the value back), read_identity, read_telemetry, features, read_buffer, capture, wait_for_state (for the encoder table, the anti-cogging and other runs), and play_events and stream_samples for sound. They are for setting up and diagnostics, not for the inside of a fast control loop. The library's examples folder shows them at work: parameters_and_status.py, capture.py, calibration_features.py, watchdog.py and sound.py.

The same release is stricter about what it sends and reads:

  • Send_Parameter takes the value itself. Parameters 8 to 16 and 20 are sent as floats (Send_Parameter(16, 1500) is 1500 mA); every other parameter takes a whole number, and anything else raises ValueError.
  • A position or a speed that does not fit 24 bits, or a current that does not fit 16 bits, raises ValueError; 1.20 wrapped it round. Send_Voltage_Limit raises ValueError outside 0 to 60000 mV.
  • A node ID must be 0 to 15.
  • UnpackData ignores frames from other nodes, remote frames and extended frames.
  • Parameters 79, 80 and 84 to 87 read as unsigned numbers.
  • A send that fails returns False and is logged once.

docs.title: Receiving
docs.text:
CanCommunication.receive_can_messages(timeout) returns (message, ids): the raw python-can message and a tuple ids with node_id, command_id and error_bit from the identifier, or (None, None) after the timeout. SpectralCAN.UnpackData(message, ids) decodes the message into the object's attributes:

Message Attributes Respond_data_pack_1 position, speed, current Respond_data_hall position, HALL_trigger, additional_pin2, hall_index Send_Respond_Encoder_data position, speed Send_Respond_Iq_data current Send_Respond_Temperature temperature Send_Respond_Voltage voltage Send_Respond_Device_Info HARDWARE_VERSION, BATCH_DATE, SOFTWARE_VERSION, SERIAL_NUMBER Send_Respond_State_of_Errors error, temperature_error, encoder_error, vbus_error, driver_error, velocity_error, current_error, estop_error, calibrated, activated, watchdog_error; from 1.21 also wrong_product Send_Respond_Identity (1.21 and newer) product_id, product_name, tool_id, firmware_version, identity_hardware_version, pole_pairs, identity_calibrated, identity_flags Send_Respond_Telemetry (1.21 and newer) temperature, voltage, the error flags as above, current Respond_Parameter (1.21 and newer) parameters[number] (floats for 8-16 and 20), unknown_parameter; tool_id and watchdog_fallback when those parameters come in Respond_Buffer_Data (1.21 and newer) capture[index], histogram[bin], cogging_harmonics[slot], cogging_table[index], encoder_table[index] Send_Respond_Kt Kt Send_Respond_Ping ping (1) Respond_Heartbeat heartbeat (1) Respond_Gripper_data_pack gripper_position, gripper_current, gripper_activated, gripper_action_status, gripper_object_detection, gripper_temperature_error, gripper_timeout_error, gripper_estop_error, gripper_calibrated

Object detection in the library

Library 1.20 and older assemble gripper_object_detection with the two bits swapped relative to the firmware, so they report 1 where the gripper sends 2 (object detected while opening) and 2 where it sends 1 (object detected while closing); 0 and 3 are unaffected. 1.21 and newer read them right.

docs.title: CAN protocol
docs.text:
CAN 2.0, 1 Mbit/s, 11-bit identifiers. The identifier carries the node ID (bits 10 to 7, 0 to 15), the command ID (bits 6 to 1, 0 to 63) and, in frames from the driver, the error bit (bit 0). Over CAN explains how the pieces are used; this page lists them.

Three kinds of message:

  • Send_… — the host sends data to the driver. A few are answered (the motion commands with Respond_data_pack_1, the gripper command with Respond_Gripper_data_pack); most are not.
  • Send_Respond_… — the host asks for data with a remote frame (RTR bit set, no data) under the command ID; the driver answers with a data frame under the same command ID.
  • Respond_… — frames only the driver sends.

Multi-byte values are big-endian (data[0] first); floats are IEEE 754 single precision; bits inside a byte are numbered from the most significant bit (bit 7 first).

docs.title: By group
docs.text:
• Motion: the motion commands and their answers, HALL homing
  • Gains and limits: the loop gains, the limits, Kt
  • Status requests: temperature, voltage, device info, errors, current, encoder, Kt, identity, telemetry, the heartbeat
  • System: node ID, E-stop, idle, save, reset, clear, watchdog, heartbeat setup, settings
  • Parameters and buffers: the parameters behind Send_Parameter and Send_Get_Parameter, every one of them, and the buffers: capture, histogram, anti-cogging, encoder table
  • Sound: tones, the queue and samples through the motor
  • Gripper: the gripper command, calibration and the gripper state

docs.title: The Python library
docs.text: Every message the host can send has a method of the same name in Spectral_BLDC.SpectralCAN, listed in Python library.

docs.title: Tools and downloads
docs.text: Build or decode a CAN frame, and download this firmware's JSON and DBC definitions.

docs.title: Gains and limits
docs.text: The commands that set the loop gains and the limits. None of them is answered; save with Send_Save_config.

docs.title: Send_PD_Gains
docs.text:
ID 16host → driver8 bytesPython: Send_PD_Gains()

Sets KP and KD, the gains of the impedance (PD) loop. Keep them with Send_Save_config.

8 bytes

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-3 KP float 32 4-7 KD float 32

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Current_Gains
docs.text:
ID 17host → driver8 bytesPython: Send_Current_Gains()

Sets Kp and Ki of the PI current loop of Iq. The Id loop keeps its gains; over UART, #Kpiq and #Kiiq set both loops, and so do parameters 11 and 12, a calibration and parameter 49.

8 bytes

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-3 Kp_iq float 32 4-7 Ki_iq float 32

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Velocity_Gains
docs.text:
ID 18host → driver8 bytesPython: Send_Velocity_Gains()

Sets Kp and Ki of the PI velocity loop.

8 bytes

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-3 Kpv float 32 4-7 Kiv float 32

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Position_Gains
docs.text:
ID 19host → driver4 bytesPython: Send_Position_Gains()

Sets Kp of the P position loop.

4 bytes

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-3 Kpp float 32

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Limits
docs.text:
ID 20host → driver8 bytesPython: Send_Limits()

Sets the speed limit and the current limit the loops may reach. From firmware 109 the current limit stops at the driver's maximum of 2800 mA, as #Ilim does, and a negative value or one that is not a number is ignored. Firmware 108 and older stored the limit as sent. Send no more than the motor's rated current.

8 bytes

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-3 Speed limit float 32 encoder ticks/s 4-7 Current limit float 32 mA

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Kt
docs.text:
ID 22host → driver4 bytesPython: Send_Kt()

Sets the motor's torque constant Kt, which the driver uses to estimate torque from current.

4 bytes

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Voltage_Limit
docs.text:
ID 34host → driver4 bytesPython: Send_Voltage_Limit()

Sets the voltage limit of the current loops (the same value as #Vlim), in mV. 0 means use the supply voltage. Added in firmware 105. From firmware 109 it takes 0 to 60000 mV, as parameter 17 does; a value outside is ignored.

4 bytes

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-3 Voltage limit signed 32-bit mV; 0 = Vbus

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Gripper
docs.text: The commands of gripper mode (#Gripper 1, saved).

docs.title: Send_gripper_data_pack
docs.text:
ID 61host → driver0 or 5 bytesPython: Send_gripper_data_pack()

The gripper command, for a driver set up as a gripper (#Gripper 1, saved). Position, speed and the current limit of the move, plus the activate, action and E-stop bits. A move is carried out only while the gripper is calibrated, activated and the action bit is 1. An empty frame (0 bytes) only asks for the state.

5 bytes

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0 Position unsigned 8-bit 0 fully open, 255 fully closed 1 Speed unsigned 8-bit 0 slowest, 255 fastest 2-3 Current signed 16-bit current limit of the move in mA; from firmware 109 the move uses its magnitude, at most the driver's 2800 mA; see the gripper manual for the safe range 4 7 Activate bit 1 activate the gripper, 0 deactivate 4 6 Action bit 1 go to the position, 0 idle 4 5 E-stop bit 1 raises the gripper E-stop error, again on every control cycle until a frame with this bit 0 arrives; then Send_Clear_Error 4 4 Release direction bit read by the firmware but not used

The driver answers with Respond_Gripper_data_pack.

docs.title: Send_gripper_calibrate
docs.text:
ID 62host → driver0 bytesPython: Send_gripper_calibrate()

Starts the gripper calibration (the jaws find their end stops). Needed after every power-up.

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Respond_Gripper_data_pack
docs.text:
ID 60driver → host4 bytes

The driver's answer to Send_gripper_data_pack: position, measured current, and the state bits. Python attributes gripper_position, gripper_current, gripper_activated, gripper_action_status, gripper_object_detection, gripper_temperature_error, gripper_timeout_error, gripper_estop_error, gripper_calibrated. The Python library 1.20 and older combine the two object-detection bits the wrong way round, so their gripper_object_detection reads 2 for an object found while closing and 1 for one found while opening; 1.21 and newer read them as the table says.

The frame (4 bytes)

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0 gripper_position unsigned 8-bit 0 fully open, 255 fully closed 1-2 gripper_current signed 16-bit measured current in mA 3 7 gripper_activated bit 1 activated 3 6 gripper_action_status bit the action bit of the last Send_gripper_data_pack (1 after #Grippos); the driver never clears it, so it stays 1 after the move ends: the object detection tells when the move has ended 3 5-4 gripper_object_detection 2 bits bit 5 is the low bit, bit 4 the high bit: 0 moving, 1 object detected while closing, 2 object detected while opening, 3 at the position 3 3 gripper_temperature_error bit a copy of the thermistor temperature error 3 2 gripper_timeout_error bit a copy of the CAN watchdog error (Send_Watchdog), not a move timeout 3 1 gripper_estop_error bit the E-stop bit of Send_gripper_data_pack (or #Gripstop 1) was set 3 0 gripper_calibrated bit 1 calibrated

docs.title: Motion
docs.text: The commands that move the motor and the frames that come back.

docs.title: Send_data_pack_1
docs.text:
ID 2host → driver2 or 5 or 8 bytesPython: Send_data_pack_1()

The motion command. Its length decides the control mode the driver enters: 8 bytes command a position with a speed and a current feedforward, 5 bytes a speed with a current feedforward, 2 bytes a current. Send 0 for a feedforward you do not use. A frame of any other length is ignored (the driver flags it as a wrong data length) but still answered.

8 bytes — position setpoint with speed and current feedforward (position mode)

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-2 Position setpoint signed 24-bit encoder ticks 3-5 Speed feedforward signed 24-bit encoder ticks/s 6-7 Current feedforward signed 16-bit mA

5 bytes — speed setpoint with current feedforward (velocity mode)

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-2 Speed setpoint signed 24-bit encoder ticks/s 3-4 Current feedforward signed 16-bit mA

2 bytes — current setpoint (current mode)

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-1 Current setpoint signed 16-bit mA

The driver answers with Respond_data_pack_1.

Every form resets the watchdog. With Rstint set, the integral accumulators are cleared on each new setpoint. From firmware 109 a position or speed frame that follows another mode (idle, current, PD, a watchdog trip) starts the velocity integral from zero, so a release from a wound-up mode does not kick; one that follows position or velocity mode keeps it. The new setpoint and the mode change reach the control loop together.

docs.title: Send_data_pack_PD
docs.text:
ID 4host → driver8 bytesPython: Send_data_pack_PD()

Puts the driver in impedance (PD) mode and sets the position, speed and current feedforward of the PD loop, whose gains are KP and KD (Send_PD_Gains).

8 bytes

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-2 Position setpoint signed 24-bit encoder ticks 3-5 Speed setpoint signed 24-bit encoder ticks/s 6-7 Current feedforward signed 16-bit mA

The driver answers with Respond_data_pack_1.

Firmware 106 and older wrote the speed into the feedforward instead of the PD loop's speed setpoint, so the speed term had no effect; 107 fixed it.

docs.title: Send_data_pack_HALL
docs.text:
ID 31host → driver4 bytesPython: Send_data_pack_HALL()

Homing against a sensor: the driver spins at the given speed until the input on the ADDITIONAL2 pin shows the trigger condition, then latches the position it reached as its position setpoint and holds it. With a level trigger (0 or 1) it holds only while the pin stays at that level: when the pin changes back, the driver spins on again until the level returns. The edge trigger (2) holds after the first edge. Sending the command again while the driver is already in HALL mode does not re-arm it; leave the mode first.

4 bytes

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-2 Speed signed 24-bit encoder ticks/s; the sign gives the direction 3 Trigger unsigned 8-bit 0 = trigger when the pin is low, 1 = when it is high, 2 = on any edge

The driver answers with Respond_data_hall.

Firmware 103 read only bit 7 of byte 3 (0 or 1); the edge trigger (2) came later.

docs.title: Respond_data_pack_1
docs.text:
ID 3driver → host8 bytes

The driver's answer to Send_data_pack_1 and Send_data_pack_PD: where the motor is, how fast it turns and the current it draws. The Python library stores them as position, speed and current.

The frame (8 bytes)

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-2 position signed 24-bit encoder ticks 3-5 speed signed 24-bit encoder ticks/s 6-7 current signed 16-bit Iq in mA

docs.title: Respond_data_hall
docs.text:
ID 32driver → host4 bytes

The driver's answer to Send_data_pack_HALL: the position and the state of the sensor input. Python attributes: position, HALL_trigger, additional_pin2, hall_index.

The frame (4 bytes)

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0-2 position signed 24-bit encoder ticks 3 7 HALL_trigger bit 1 while the driver waits for the trigger (with a level trigger, also again after the pin left the level), 0 while it holds 3 6 additional_pin2 bit the raw level of the ADDITIONAL2 pin 3 5 hall_index bit 1 once the trigger has been seen (latched)

docs.title: Send_data_pack_2
docs.text:
ID 6host → drivernot implemented

Reserved. The firmware has no handler for this ID and the Python library's call does nothing.

docs.title: Send_data_pack_3
docs.text:
ID 8host → drivernot implemented

Reserved. The firmware has no handler for this ID and the Python library's call does nothing.

docs.title: Respond_data_pack_2
docs.text:
ID 5driver → host0 bytes

Reserved; the driver never sends it.

docs.title: Respond_data_pack_3
docs.text:
ID 7driver → host0 bytes

Reserved; the driver never sends it.

docs.title: Send_Iq
docs.text:
ID 21host → drivernot implemented

Reserved; the firmware has no handler for this ID. Use the 2-byte form of Send_data_pack_1 for a current setpoint.

docs.title: Parameters and buffers
docs.text:
From firmware 109 a setting that has no command of its own is a parameter: a number from 1 to 87 behind one pair of commands, Send_Parameter (ID 36) to set it and Send_Get_Parameter (ID 37) to read it, answered with Respond_Parameter (ID 38). The identifier has room for only 64 command IDs, so new settings no longer use them up. Parameter numbers are permanent: a number is never given a new meaning. Number 73 is not used and stays free.

The buffers are the larger data a drive holds: a capture of three signals, a histogram, the anti-cogging set and the encoder table. Send_Buffer_Read (ID 41) reads them in 8-byte frames, Respond_Buffer_Data (ID 42) carries them, and Send_Buffer_Write (ID 43) writes the anti-cogging set.

Over UART, #Par does the same: #Par lists every parameter, #Par 56 reads one, #Par 56,0 sets it (Status and utility).

docs.title: Setting and reading a parameter
docs.text:
A set is not answered: read the value back to know what the driver took. A value outside a parameter's range is clamped, replaced or refused, as the table says, and a read-only number ignores the write.

import Spectral_BLDC as Spectral

comms = Spectral.CanCommunication(bustype='slcan', channel='COM41', bitrate=1000000)
motor = Spectral.SpectralCAN(node_id=0, communication=comms)

motor.Send_Parameter(56, 0)                # nothing runs by itself after the next #Calangle
motor.Send_Get_Parameter(56)               # read it back
message, ids = comms.receive_can_messages(timeout=0.1)
if message is not None:
    motor.UnpackData(message, ids)
print(motor.parameters.get(56))
motor.Send_Save_config()                   # keep it over a power cycle

Send_Parameter, Send_Get_Parameter and the buffer calls need the Spectral-BLDC library 1.21 or newer. Send_Parameter takes the value itself: a gain or a limit (8 to 16 and 20) is sent as a float, so motor.Send_Parameter(16, 1500) sets a current limit of 1500 mA; every other parameter takes a whole number.

docs.title: Send_Parameter
docs.text:
ID 36host → driver5 bytesPython: Send_Parameter()

Sets one parameter by its number (the parameter table). Firmware 109 gives new settings a parameter number instead of a command ID of their own, since the identifier has room for only 64 command IDs. A value outside a parameter's range is clamped, replaced or refused as the table says; a number the firmware does not know, or a read-only one, is ignored. The driver does not answer: read the value back with Send_Get_Parameter. A value set this way lives in RAM until Send_Save_config, like every other setting; the table says which parameters Save keeps.

5 bytes

Byte Field Type Meaning 0 Parameter unsigned 8-bit the parameter number, 1-87 1-4 Value signed 32-bit the new value, in the parameter's unit; for the gains, limits and Kt (8-16, 20) a float's bit pattern

The driver does not answer this command.

A data frame of another length, or a remote frame, is ignored and flagged as a wrong data length. It does not reset the watchdog.

docs.title: Send_Get_Parameter
docs.text:
ID 37host → driver1 bytesPython: Send_Get_Parameter()

Asks for the value in force of one parameter. The answer, Respond_Parameter, comes under ID 38, not 37: a host and a driver must never send data frames with the same identifier, because two sent at the same moment collide. Resets the watchdog. The Python library stores the value in parameters[number].

1 bytes

Byte Field Type Meaning 0 Parameter unsigned 8-bit the parameter number

The driver answers with Respond_Parameter.

docs.title: Respond_Parameter
docs.text:
ID 38driver → host5 bytes

The answer to Send_Get_Parameter: the number and the value in force. For a number the firmware does not know the frame carries the number alone (1 byte; the Python library sets unknown_parameter). The gains, limits and Kt (parameters 8 to 16 and 20) travel as the bit pattern of an IEEE-754 float, the others as integers.

The frame (5 bytes)

Byte Field Type Meaning 0 parameter unsigned 8-bit the parameter number 1-4 value signed 32-bit the value in force; a float's bits for 8-16 and 20

docs.title: Send_Buffer_Read
docs.text:
ID 41host → driver5 bytesPython: Send_Buffer_Read()

Asks for entries of one of the drive's buffers: the capture, the histogram, the anti-cogging harmonics or table, or the encoder table. The driver answers with one Respond_Buffer_Data frame per entry (for the two tables, one per three values), sent from its main loop whenever a transmit mailbox is free, so a long read-out never holds up the control loop or other answers. A new request replaces one still in progress; count 0 cancels it. Entries past the end are not sent. Resets the watchdog.

5 bytes

Byte Field Type Meaning 0 Kind unsigned 8-bit 0 capture (up to 1024 samples: parameter 32 says how many), 1 histogram (256 bins), 2 anti-cogging harmonics (8 slots), 3 anti-cogging table (256 values), 4 encoder table (128 values) 1-2 First unsigned 16-bit the first index 3-4 Count unsigned 16-bit how many entries; 0 cancels a read-out

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Respond_Buffer_Data
docs.text:
ID 42driver → host8 bytes

One entry of a buffer, the answer to Send_Buffer_Read. The first two bytes say which: the kind in the top three bits, the index in the other thirteen (kind × 8192 + index). The six bytes after them depend on the kind, as the table below the frame says.

The frame (8 bytes)

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-1 header unsigned 16-bit kind × 8192 + index 2-3 word_a signed 16-bit capture: channel A; histogram: the count (unsigned); harmonics: the harmonic number (0 = slot unused); tables: entry index 4-5 word_b signed 16-bit capture: channel B; histogram: the sum's upper 16 bits; harmonics: a, the cosine term in mA; tables: entry index + 1 6-7 word_c signed 16-bit capture: channel C; histogram: the sum's lower 16 bits; harmonics: b, the sine term in mA; tables: entry index + 2 (0 past the end) Kind Index Bytes 2-7 0 capture the sample, oldest first, 0 to parameter 32 − 1 channels A, B and C, each in its signal's unit (the parameter table lists the signals) 1 histogram the bin, 0-255 over one electrical turn or one motor turn the count (unsigned 16-bit), then the sum (signed 32-bit); the bin's mean is sum ÷ count 2 anti-cogging harmonics the slot, 0-7 the harmonic of the electrical angle (1-32, 0 = unused), a and b in mA: the slot adds a·cos(h·θ) + b·sin(h·θ) 3 anti-cogging table the first of three values, 0-255 three values in mA, 64 angle counts apart (256 per electrical turn) 4 encoder table the first of three values, 0-127 three corrections in 1/16 encoder count, 128 per motor turn

docs.title: Reading the capture
docs.text:
A capture records three signals inside the control loop, one sample every divider loops, 1024 samples per channel. It starts when parameter 28 is written: at once (1), when the error flag rises (2, a watchdog trip included), or when channel A rises (3) or falls (4) through the level of parameter 29. Parameter 30 keeps that many samples from before the trigger. Status and diagnostics shows a whole capture.

  1. Set the signals (24, 25, 26), the divider (27), the pre-trigger (30) and, for 3 and 4, the level (29).
  2. Write the trigger (28). Parameter 31 reads 1 (armed), 2 (recording), then 3 (done).
  3. Read parameter 32 (samples readable) and 33 (the trigger sample's index, −1 if none).
  4. Send_Buffer_Read with kind 0, first 0, count = parameter 32: one Respond_Buffer_Data frame per sample, oldest first.

The histogram works the same way with parameters 34 to 36 and kind 1: it adds a signal into 256 bins by the electrical angle or by the encoder, every control loop, until it is stopped or one bin holds 65535 samples.

docs.title: Sound
docs.text: Sound through the motor: tones, a queue of timed events and samples, added to the output voltage while the driver holds or moves. Sound explains how to use them; parameters 80 to 82 are in the parameter table.

docs.title: Send_Sound
docs.text:
ID 44host → driver8 bytesPython: Send_Sound()

Plays sound through the motor: a tone now, a queue of timed events, or samples. The sound is added to the output voltage, on the q axis by default (parameter 82), and only while the driver holds or moves (position, velocity, current or PD mode); idle or an error stops all of it. Up to 4 tones sound at once (channels 0 to 3), from 20 Hz to below 3125 Hz, half the control-loop rate. Loudness is given as a current: the driver turns it into a voltage with the coil's impedance at that pitch, so low and high notes sound alike. The total voltage is limited to parameter 81 (2000 mV by default; 0 refuses sound). Added in firmware 109. The driver does not answer; parameter 80 says what plays. The Python library wraps the operations as Send_Tone, Send_Sound_Stop, Send_Sound_Event, Send_Sound_Play, Send_Sound_Clear, Send_Samples_Play and Send_Samples_Stop.

8 bytes

Byte Field Type Meaning 0 Operation unsigned 8-bit 0 stop everything (tones, queue, samples); 1 a tone now; 2 add an event to the queue; 3 play the queue; 4 play the samples; 5 samples off, buffer cleared; 6 clear the queue (tones that sound keep sounding) 1 Channel unsigned 8-bit the tone channel, 0-3 (operations 1 and 2) 2-3 A unsigned 16-bit 1, 2: the pitch in Hz (2: 0 silences the channel); 4: the sample rate in Hz, at most the loop rate 4-5 B unsigned 16-bit 1, 2: the loudness in mA; 4: the voltage of a full-scale sample in mV 6-7 C unsigned 16-bit 1: the duration in ms, 0 = until stopped; 2: the wait in ms before the next event, 0 = the next one starts with it

The driver does not answer this command.

The queue holds 31 events and is played by the control loop with loop-exact timing: an event sets one channel's pitch and loudness, then waits. A chord is three events with wait 0 and a fourth with the chord's length. When the queue runs out, every channel falls silent. An event sent to a full queue is dropped. Samples: send them first with Send_Sound_Samples, then operation 4; the driver plays them at the given rate and stops when the buffer runs dry. A frame of another length, or a remote frame, is ignored. It does not reset the watchdog.

docs.title: Send_Sound_Samples
docs.text:
ID 45host → driver1 to 8 bytesPython: Send_Samples()

Appends 1 to 8 samples (signed 8-bit, one per byte, −127 to 127 = full scale) to the driver's 1024-place sample buffer, which holds 1023 samples. Samples that do not fit are dropped; parameter 80 says how many are buffered. Send_Sound with operation 4 plays them. Added in firmware 109. The driver does not answer.

8 bytes — eight samples; a shorter frame carries fewer

Byte Field Type Meaning 0 Sample 1 signed 8-bit the next sample 1 Sample 2 signed 8-bit 2 Sample 3 signed 8-bit 3 Sample 4 signed 8-bit 4 Sample 5 signed 8-bit 5 Sample 6 signed 8-bit 6 Sample 7 signed 8-bit 7 Sample 8 signed 8-bit

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Status requests
docs.text: Data the host asks for with a remote frame (RTR bit set, no data); the driver answers with a data frame with the same command ID. And the heartbeat, which the driver sends on its own.

docs.title: Send_Respond_Ping
docs.text:
ID 10host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frameremote frame, 0 bytesPython: Send_Respond_Ping()

Asks the driver to answer with an empty frame, to see that it is on the bus.

The frame (0 bytes) carries no data.

The driver answers with Send_Respond_Ping.

docs.title: Send_Respond_Temperature
docs.text:
ID 23host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frameremote frame, 0 bytesPython: Send_Respond_Temperature()

Asks for the thermistor temperature. Meaningful only with the thermistor enabled (#Term 1).

The frame (2 bytes)

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-1 temperature signed 16-bit °C

The driver answers with Send_Respond_Temperature.

docs.title: Send_Respond_Voltage
docs.text:
ID 24host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frameremote frame, 0 bytesPython: Send_Respond_Voltage()

Asks for the supply voltage.

The frame (2 bytes)

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-1 voltage unsigned 16-bit mV

The driver answers with Send_Respond_Voltage.

docs.title: Send_Respond_Device_Info
docs.text:
ID 25host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frameremote frame, 0 bytesPython: Send_Respond_Device_Info()

Asks for the driver's identity: hardware version and batch date from the EEPROM, the serial number, and the firmware release (from firmware 105 on this is the build's own version; before, a value from the EEPROM). This firmware does not read the serial number back from the EEPROM at power-up: it reports 1 until #SERNUM sets it.

The frame (7 bytes)

Byte Field Type Meaning 0 HARDWARE_VERSION unsigned 8-bit PCB revision 1 BATCH_DATE unsigned 8-bit production batch 2 SOFTWARE_VERSION unsigned 8-bit firmware release, e.g. 108 3-6 SERIAL_NUMBER unsigned 32-bit serial number as held in RAM: 1 after a power-up

The driver answers with Send_Respond_Device_Info.

docs.title: Send_Respond_State_of_Errors
docs.text:
ID 26host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frameremote frame, 0 bytesPython: Send_Respond_State_of_Errors()

Asks for every error flag and the calibrated, activated, watchdog and product-lock states.

The frame (2 bytes)

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0 7 error bit any error is active 0 6 temperature_error bit motor over the temperature limit 0 5 encoder_error bit the encoder reports no magnet (too weak a field) 0 4 vbus_error bit supply voltage outside the limits 0 3 driver_error bit reserved; never set by this firmware (STEPFOC does not read a fault output of its driver stage) 0 2 velocity_error bit speed above 30,000,000 ticks/s, a fixed threshold (not #Vlimit) 0 1 current_error bit reserved; never set by this firmware 0 0 estop_error bit Send_ESTOP was received 1 7 calibrated bit the motor is calibrated 1 6 activated bit the controller is activated 1 5 watchdog_error bit the watchdog ran out 1 4 wrong_product bit from firmware 109: this firmware is on the other product's board (the product lock) and drives nothing

The driver answers with Send_Respond_State_of_Errors.

docs.title: Send_Respond_Iq_data
docs.text:
ID 27host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frameremote frame, 0 bytesPython: Send_Respond_Iq_data()

Asks for the measured Iq current.

The frame (2 bytes)

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-1 current signed 16-bit mA

The driver answers with Send_Respond_Iq_data.

docs.title: Send_Respond_Encoder_data
docs.text:
ID 28host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frameremote frame, 0 bytesPython: Send_Respond_Encoder_data()

Asks for the position and the filtered speed, as 32-bit values. Python attributes position and speed.

The frame (8 bytes)

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-3 position signed 32-bit encoder ticks 4-7 speed signed 32-bit encoder ticks/s

The driver answers with Send_Respond_Encoder_data.

docs.title: Send_Respond_Kt
docs.text:
ID 33host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frameremote frame, 0 bytesPython: Send_Respond_Kt()

Asks for the torque constant Kt the driver uses. Added in firmware 105.

The frame (4 bytes)

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-3 Kt float 32 Nm/A

The driver answers with Send_Respond_Kt.

docs.title: Send_Respond_Identity
docs.text:
ID 39host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frameremote frame, 0 bytesPython: Send_Respond_Identity()

Asks what the drive is: the product, the tool it is built into, the firmware release, the hardware version, the pole pairs, whether it is calibrated, and eight flags. A host can check it before it commands or flashes a drive. Added in firmware 109. Python attributes product_id, product_name, tool_id, firmware_version, identity_hardware_version, pole_pairs, identity_calibrated, identity_flags.

The frame (8 bytes)

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0 product unsigned 8-bit 1 STEPFOC, 2 Spectral Micro: the firmware that answers 1 tool_id unsigned 8-bit parameter 1: 0 none, 1 SSG-48, 11-33 MSG, 200-254 your own 2-3 firmware_version unsigned 16-bit the release, e.g. 109 4 hardware_version unsigned 8-bit PCB revision from the EEPROM 5 pole_pairs unsigned 8-bit the motor's pole pairs; 0 if outside 0-255 6 calibrated unsigned 8-bit 1 calibrated, 0 not 7 0 gripper bit the driver is set up as a gripper (#Gripper 1) 7 1 brake_on_idle bit idle brakes (1) or coasts (0) 7 2 commutation_reversed bit calibration found the coils wired the other way round 7 3 settings_block2 bit the EEPROM has the bank settings block 2 lives in, so parameters 1-5 can be saved 7 4 wrong_product bit this firmware is on the other product's board (the product lock) and drives nothing 7 5 sense_zero_measured bit the current-sense zero was measured at start-up and is plausible 7 6 cogging_saved bit the anti-cogging in use is the one saved in the EEPROM 7 7 switching_zero_in_use bit the current-sense zero measured with the bridge switching is in use (parameter 46)

The driver answers with Send_Respond_Identity.

The flags in byte 7 are numbered the usual way, bit 0 the least significant (unlike the error bytes, which the firmware packs from bit 7 down).

docs.title: Send_Respond_Telemetry
docs.text:
ID 40host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frameremote frame, 0 bytesPython: Send_Respond_Telemetry()

Asks for the temperature, the supply voltage, both error bytes and the current in one frame, all from the same moment: one request instead of four. Added in firmware 109. The Python library fills the same attributes as the four separate answers.

The frame (8 bytes)

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-1 temperature signed 16-bit °C (meaningful with the thermistor enabled) 2-3 voltage signed 16-bit supply voltage in mV 4 errors_1 unsigned 8-bit the error flags, as byte 0 of Send_Respond_State_of_Errors 5 errors_2 unsigned 8-bit calibrated, activated, watchdog, wrong product, as byte 1 of Send_Respond_State_of_Errors 6-7 current signed 16-bit Iq in mA

The driver answers with Send_Respond_Telemetry.

docs.title: Respond_Heartbeat
docs.text:
ID 9driver → host0 bytes

The frame the driver sends on its own at the heartbeat interval (Send_Heartbeat_Setup); empty. Off by default. Any other frame the driver sends resets the heartbeat timer, so a driver that answers motion commands at a high rate never sends a heartbeat.

The frame (0 bytes) carries no data.

docs.title: System
docs.text: Identity, saving, resetting, errors, the watchdog, the heartbeat and the settings.

docs.title: Send_CAN_ID
docs.text:
ID 11host → driver1 bytesPython: Send_CAN_ID()

Gives the driver a new node ID, 0 to 13 (the firmware accepts up to 15, but the bootloader reserves 14 and 15: a driver on one of those cannot be updated over CAN). Saving the configuration (Send_Save_config) also writes the ID into the bootloader's board ID. The driver answers to the new ID at once; the ID is kept over a power cycle only after Send_Save_config.

1 bytes

Byte Field Type Meaning 0 ID unsigned 8-bit 0 to 13; 14 and 15 are accepted but reserved by the bootloader

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_ESTOP
docs.text:
ID 0host → driver0 bytesPython: Send_ESTOP()

Stops the motor and raises the E-stop error, which stays until Send_Clear_Error.

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Idle
docs.text:
ID 12host → driver0 bytesPython: Send_Idle()

Puts the driver in idle mode (the motor coasts or brakes, see Send_Settings).

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Save_config
docs.text:
ID 13host → driver0 bytesPython: Send_Save_config()

Writes the current configuration (gains, limits, calibration, CAN ID, heartbeat, watchdog, gripper flag) to the EEPROM, and the CAN ID into the bootloader's board ID. From firmware 109 it also writes the tool id and the watchdog fallback (settings block 2), the anti-cogging set with its mode and scale, and the encoder table with its on/off flag, parameter 56 and the current-sense zero trims, each block with its own checksum; of the two large blocks only the 16-byte pages that changed are written. Not kept: the idle behaviour of Send_Settings, the current loop bandwidth, and every parameter the parameter table marks as not kept. It also writes the serial number held in RAM, which is 1 after a power-up unless #SERNUM set it, over the stored one. A drive stopped by the product lock writes nothing.

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Reset
docs.text:
ID 14host → driver0 bytesPython: Send_Reset()

Resets the driver. From firmware 105 the reset lands in the bootloader, which waits 2 s for a flashing host and then starts the firmware again; this is how a firmware update begins.

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Clear_Error
docs.text:
ID 1host → driver0 bytesPython: Send_Clear_Error()

Clears the error flags and goes to idle; it also ends a watchdog hold or descend. An error whose cause is still present comes straight back. A calibration error is cleared only by calibrating. A gripper E-stop comes back until the E-stop bit of Send_gripper_data_pack is 0 again.

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Watchdog
docs.text:
ID 15host → driver5 bytesPython: Send_Watchdog()

Sets the watchdog: when the time runs out the driver reports a watchdog error and does what the action byte says. Every valid motion frame (Send_data_pack_1, Send_data_pack_PD, Send_data_pack_HALL, Send_gripper_data_pack) and every request the driver answers (status requests, Send_Get_Parameter, Send_Buffer_Read) resets it. From firmware 109 so do Send_Save_config and Send_Watchdog itself, which starts a fresh window. The other setting frames (gains, limits, Idle, Clear, Settings, Send_Parameter) do not. 0 turns it off (the default). From firmware 109 the driver acts on the action byte, but only when the watchdog is the only active error: any other error gets the legacy response. Hold and descend run for the fallback time (parameter 2, 2 s by default), then the after-action (parameter 5); they start only if the driver was in position, velocity, current, PD or gripper mode, otherwise it stays as idle was. The watchdog explains each action. Send_Save_config keeps the watchdog, and a kept watchdog runs from power-up: a host that sends nothing within the time finds the driver in watchdog error, and clears it with Send_Clear_Error. The same values are parameters 6 and 7.

5 bytes

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-3 Time unsigned 32-bit ms; 0 = off 4 Action unsigned 8-bit 0 legacy (brake or coast as idle does), 1 hold the position, 2 brake, 3 coast, 4 descend at the fallback current and speed; other values act as 0

The driver does not answer this command.

Firmware 108 and older store the action byte without acting on it. The Python library sends all five actions from 1.21 ('Idle', 'Hold', 'Brake', 'Coast', 'Descend'); 1.20 and older send only 0, 1 or 2.

docs.title: Send_Heartbeat_Setup
docs.text:
ID 30host → driver4 bytesPython: Send_Heartbeat_Setup()

Sets the heartbeat interval in ms; 0 turns the heartbeat off (the default). Kept by Send_Save_config.

4 bytes

Byte Field Type Meaning 0-3 Interval unsigned 32-bit ms; 0 = off

docs.title: Send_Settings
docs.text:
ID 35host → driver2 to 8 bytes

Sets boolean settings that have no command of their own: a mask byte says which settings the frame touches, a value byte gives their new values; settings outside the mask are left alone. Bit 0 is the idle behaviour: 1 brake (phases shorted), 0 coast. The setting is not kept by Send_Save_config: at power-up the driver brakes. Added in firmware 107. The Python library has Send_Settings and Send_Brake_Coast from 1.21; 1.20 and older have no call for it.

2 bytes

Byte Field Type Meaning 0 Mask unsigned 8-bit bit 0 = write the idle behaviour 1 Value unsigned 8-bit bit 0: 1 brake, 0 coast

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Cyclic_command
docs.text:
ID 29host → drivernot implemented

Reserved. The firmware has no handler for this ID and the Python library's call does nothing.

docs.title: UART commands
docs.text: Every command the firmware release this site describes understands over the serial port. The kind, the argument type, the mode a command enters and what it prints are read from the firmware; the descriptions are written by hand. Over UART explains the protocol.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
#<Name> [number]
  • A Set/Get command sets the value when a number follows and prints the current value either way.
  • A Get command only prints.
  • An Action command does something; a number after it is ignored. (In firmware 108 and older #Idle and #PWM with a number were answered Unknown command.)
  • Names are case-sensitive, at most 19 characters; the argument is one word of at most 19 characters, without spaces, so a list is written with commas (#WdFb 2000,0,1000,2, #Par 56,0); the line ends with LF (CR before it is fine). Firmware 108 and older allowed 20 characters for name and number together. 256000 baud, 8N1, 3.3 V.
  • A name the firmware does not know is answered Unknown command.

docs.title: By group
docs.text:
• Motion: setpoints and modes
  • Gains and limits: the loop gains, the limits, the integrator reset, the current loop bandwidth
  • Calibration and motor parameters: Cal and Calonly, the motor's R, L and pole pairs, the constants calibration finds, the calibration settings, the encoder table (Encal) and the anti-cogging (Cogcal)
  • Status and utility: save, reset, defaults, identity, errors, temperature, the cyclic output, any parameter (Par), the tool id, the watchdog fallback, the product lock
  • Gripper: gripper mode

docs.title: Calibration and motor parameters
docs.text: #Cal #Calonly #Calangle #Encal #Cogcal #R #L #PP #Kt #KV #Flux #Offset #Iqoffset #Magnet #Dir #Phase #Resv #Calpwr #Openv #Opens #Vp #Calibrated

docs.title: #Cal
docs.text:
ActionEnters idle mode

Runs the calibration routine (see Motor parameters and calibration), over the serial port only. Enter R, L and PP first, and the current limit for the motor: it uses its own 1600 mA for its steps and puts the limit back when it ends (firmware 108 and older left 1600 mA). From firmware 109, when it succeeds, the encoder table and then the anti-cogging with the current-sense trim follow by themselves, and everything is saved (about a minute; keep the shaft free).

Response: the calibration log

docs.title: #Calonly
docs.text:
ActionEnters idle mode

The calibration alone: like Cal, but nothing follows it. Save afterwards with Save. Added in firmware 109.

Response: the calibration log

docs.title: #Calangle
docs.text:
ActionEnters angle-offset calibration mode

Runs only an angle-offset search. It uses an older routine than the one in Cal, which gives up after about two minutes and keeps the offset it reached. Prints Idle at once, before the search starts. From firmware 109, when parameter 56 is not 0, the anti-cogging is identified again afterwards (with the current-sense trim) and everything is saved: the anti-cogging depends on the offset. After a timeout nothing follows and nothing is saved. From firmware 109 it is refused while the driver is in error.

Response: Idle, at once; Calangle: not started, the drive is in error (#Error, #Clear) when it is refused

docs.title: #Encal
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument nothing, or save, all, stop, on, off, state

The encoder table (see Encoder table and anti-cogging). Alone it measures the table and uses it: the field turns the rotor open loop one shaft turn each way at 2048 ticks/s, about 20 s, with the shaft free. save also saves; all then identifies the anti-cogging and saves both; stop aborts; on and off switch the correction (on only with a measured table, and neither while a run turns the motor); state, or any other word, only prints. The same as parameters 52 and 53. Added in firmware 109.

Response: Encoder table: <state>, then the table's error in degrees

docs.title: #Cogcal
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument nothing, or save, trim, stop, state

The anti-cogging identification on the drive (see Encoder table and anti-cogging): one motor turn forward and one back in velocity mode at parameter 44's speed (1500 ticks/s, about 22 s), the shaft free to turn. save also saves; trim first corrects the current-sense zeros from the result and identifies again (not saved: parameter 43 = 5 trims and saves); stop aborts, also the encoder part of a combined run; state, or any other word, only prints. States 10 and 11 print their own text; 7 and 8, the encoder part of a combined run, show only in parameter 43. Added in firmware 109.

Response: Anti-cogging identification: <state>, the speed and the identified cogging in mA rms, and the harmonics when done

docs.title: #R
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument float: resistance in Ω

The phase resistance of the motor (one coil). STEPFOC does not measure it; enter the datasheet value before Cal. Also parameter 76, in mΩ.

Response: the current value

docs.title: #L
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument float: inductance in H

The phase inductance of the motor (one coil); enter the datasheet value before Cal. Also parameter 77, in µH.

Response: the current value

docs.title: #PP
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: pole pairs

The motor's pole pairs: 50 for a 1.8° stepper, 75 for 1.2°, 100 for 0.9°, 125 for 0.72°. Calibration accepts only these values. Also parameter 78: 1-200, only while idle; from 109 #PP answers PP: not taken (1-200, and only while idle) otherwise.

Response: the current value

docs.title: #Kt
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument float: Nm/A

The torque constant, found by calibration.

Response: the current value

docs.title: #KV
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument float: rpm/V

The velocity constant, found by calibration.

Response: the current value

docs.title: #Flux
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument float: Wb

The flux linkage, found by calibration. Works over UART from firmware 109; the parser of 108 and older accepted only the lowercase #flux, which had no handler.

Response: the current value

docs.title: #Offset
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument float: angle in rad

The angle offset between encoder zero and electrical zero, found by calibration.

Response: the current value

docs.title: #Iqoffset
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: current in mA

The current used by the angle-offset search.

Response: the current value

docs.title: #Magnet
docs.text:
Get

Reads the encoder's magnet status.

Response: Magnet Good or Magnet Bad

docs.title: #Dir
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: 0 or 1

A stored flag that Info prints as Phase direction. The control code does not use it in this release; #Default writes 0.

Response: the current value

docs.title: #Phase
docs.text:
Get

Prints the phase order found by calibration.

Response: Phase order is: N

docs.title: #Resv
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: voltage in mV

The voltage calibration starts the resistance test at (not used by STEPFOC, which does not measure resistance).

Response: the current value

docs.title: #Calpwr
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument float: power in W

The power calibration may dissipate in the resistance and inductance tests (not used by STEPFOC).

Response: the current value

docs.title: #Openv
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: voltage in mV

The voltage of the open-loop modes (Openloop, gosteps), 5000 mV at power-up. Calibration does not use it: its open-loop spin has a fixed 5000 mV. Not kept by Save.

Response: the current value

docs.title: #Opens
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument float: electrical speed in rad/s

The electrical speed of Openloop, the same value Openloop sets. Calibration does not use it.

Response: the current value

docs.title: #Vp
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: voltage in mV

Stored, but not used by this firmware: the phase-order check of calibration uses a fixed 3000 mV.

Response: the current value

docs.title: #Calibrated
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: 0 or 1

The calibrated flag. #Calibrated 1 clears a calibration error without calibrating; the motor may still be uncalibrated.

Response: the flag

docs.title: #Vlimit
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: speed in encoder ticks/s

The speed limit: it clamps the speed setpoint of the velocity loop, and in position mode the speed the position loop asks for. The velocity integrator is clamped to the current limit (Ilim), not to this. From firmware 109 a negative number counts as its magnitude.

Response: the current limit

docs.title: #Ilim
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: current in mA

The Iq current limit, 1700 mA after #Default. Set it to the rated phase current of your motor; this command clamps it to 2800 mA and takes the magnitude of a negative number (from firmware 109 Send_Limits over CAN stops at 2800 mA too). Calibration uses 1600 mA for its steps and, from firmware 109, puts it back when it ends.

Response: the current limit

docs.title: #Vlim
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: voltage in mV

The voltage limit of the current loops (Ud and Uq), 6000 mV by default. It keeps the loops of low-resistance steppers stable, and it also caps the top speed. 0, or a value above the supply voltage, means the supply voltage.

Response: the current limit in mV

docs.title: #Rstint
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: 0 or 1

Whether the integral accumulators are reset on every new setpoint.

Response: the setting

docs.title: #Cbw
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument float: bandwidth in Hz, 10 to 625

The current loop bandwidth. From firmware 109 setting it computes Kpiq and Kiiq at once from R and L, the way calibration does, and prints them (the same as parameter 49); a value outside 10-625, or with R or L at 0, changes nothing. Not kept by Save: 160 Hz at every power-up, but the gains it set are kept.

Response: the bandwidth, then Kp_iq = …, Ki_iq = …

docs.title: Gripper
docs.text: #Gripper #Gripcal #Grippos #Gripvel #Gripcur #Gripact #Gripstop #Gripinfo

Set/GetArgument int: 0 or 1

Whether this driver is a gripper. Save it; #Default clears it.

Response: the flag

docs.title: #Gripcal
docs.text:
ActionEnters gripper calibration mode

Starts the gripper calibration: the jaws find their end stops at 500 mA. It prints nothing when it ends; after about 24 s without both end stops it gives up, uncalibrated. Gripinfo shows the result.

Response: Gripper calibration!

docs.title: #Grippos
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: 0 (open) to 255 (closed)Enters gripper mode

The position setpoint; also activates the gripper, sets the action bit and goes to gripper mode.

Response: the current position

docs.title: #Gripvel
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: 0 to 255

The speed setpoint of gripper moves, 50 at power-up.

Response: the setpoint

docs.title: #Gripcur
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: current in mA

The current limit of gripper moves, 400 mA at power-up. From firmware 109 a move uses its magnitude, at most the driver's 2800 mA (108 and older used it as sent); see the gripper manual for the safe range.

Response: the setpoint

docs.title: #Gripact
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: 0 or 1

The activate bit.

Response: the bit

docs.title: #Gripstop
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: 0 or 1

The gripper E-stop bit. While it is 1 the driver raises the gripper E-stop error on every control cycle: set it to 0, then Clear.

Response: the bit

docs.title: #Gripinfo
docs.text:
Get

Prints the gripper state: calibrated, activated, end stops, position, current.

Response: the report

docs.title: Motion
docs.text: #Iq #Id #V #P #PD #PDV #PDI #Uq #Ud #Openloop #gosteps #stepinterval #microstep #HALL #Idle #Brake #Coast #Close

docs.title: #Iq
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument float: current setpoint in mAEnters current mode

Current (torque) control with the given Iq setpoint.

Response: the measured Iq in mA

docs.title: #Id
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument float: current setpoint in mA

Sets the Id setpoint; normally left at 0. Also parameter 58.

Response: the measured Id in mA

docs.title: #V
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: speed setpoint in encoder ticks/sEnters velocity mode

Velocity control with the given speed.

Response: the measured speed in ticks/s

docs.title: #P
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: position setpoint in encoder ticksEnters position mode

Position control to the given position.

Response: the measured position in ticks

docs.title: #PD
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: position setpoint in encoder ticksEnters PD mode

Impedance (PD) control around the given position with the gains KP and KD.

Response: the measured position in ticks

docs.title: #PDV
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: speed setpoint in encoder ticks/s

The speed setpoint of the PD loop.

Response: the PD speed setpoint

docs.title: #PDI
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: current feedforward in mA

The current feedforward of the PD loop.

Response: the PD current feedforward

docs.title: #Uq
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: voltage in mVEnters voltage torque mode

Voltage-torque mode with the given q-axis voltage (no current loop).

Response: the Uq setpoint in mV

docs.title: #Ud
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: voltage in mV

The d-axis voltage used in voltage-torque mode; does not change the mode.

Response: the Ud setpoint in mV

docs.title: #Openloop
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument float: electrical speed in rad/sEnters open loop mode

Spins the motor open loop, as a plain stepper, with the voltage set by Openv. The voltage is not current-controlled and Ilim does not apply: see Open-loop stepping on Control modes.

Response: the open-loop speed

docs.title: #gosteps
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: number of microsteps (sign = direction)Enters open-loop steps mode

Moves the given number of microsteps open loop, one every stepinterval, at the voltage set by Openv, then goes to idle. With microstep 16, 16 steps are one electrical cycle: four full steps, 7.2° on a 1.8° motor.

Response: Moving for N steps

docs.title: #stepinterval
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: step time in µs

The time between two microsteps of gosteps, 1000 µs by default. It is rounded down to whole control cycles of 160 µs, and is 160 µs at the least.

Response: the step interval

docs.title: #microstep
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: microsteps per electrical cycle

The microsteps gosteps makes per electrical cycle (four full steps), 16 by default.

Response: the microstep setting

docs.title: #HALL
docs.text:
ActionEnters HALL mode

Homing against the sensor on ADDITIONAL2 at 3000 ticks/s, triggered when the pin is low. It holds while the pin stays low and spins on when the pin goes high again (see Send_data_pack_HALL for the CAN form with a chosen speed and trigger).

Response: HALL

docs.title: #Idle
docs.text:
Get

Goes to idle; the motor coasts or brakes as set by Brake / Coast.

Response: Idle

docs.title: #Brake
docs.text:
ActionEnters idle mode

Goes to idle with the motor braking (phases shorted); also the idle behaviour from then on. Not kept by Save: the driver brakes at every power-up.

Response: Brake 1

docs.title: #Coast
docs.text:
ActionEnters idle mode

Goes to idle with the motor coasting (phases open); also the idle behaviour until the next power-up, which brakes again. Not kept by Save.

Response: Coast 0

docs.title: #Close
docs.text:
ActionEnters idle mode

Leaves open loop and goes back to closed-loop idle.

Response: nothing

docs.title: Status and utility
docs.text: #Save #Reset #Default #Pullconfig #Info #Tone #Par #Tool #WdFb #Product #Param #Help #Error #Clear #Mode #Vbus #Vmax #Temp #Term #Tlim #Iabc #PWM #LED #CANID #SERNUM #Activate #Cyc #Cyca

docs.title: #Save
docs.text:
Action

Writes the configuration to the EEPROM, and the CAN ID into the bootloader's board ID. Do it after calibration and after tuning. It also writes the serial number held in RAM (1 after a power-up, unless SERNUM set it) over the stored one.

Response: Save

docs.title: #Reset
docs.text:
Action

Resets the driver. From firmware 105 the reset lands in the bootloader, which waits 2 s for a flashing host and then starts the firmware again.

Response: nothing

docs.title: #Default
docs.text:
Action

Writes the factory defaults to the EEPROM and loads them: the serial number, hardware version and batch date; the gripper flag, heartbeat, watchdog and thermistor (off); the motor parameters and the calibration (cleared); every gain and limit; from firmware 109 also the tool id (0), the watchdog fallback, the calibration ID (0), the anti-cogging set, the encoder table and its trims (cleared), and parameter 56 (back to 2). From firmware 109 the CAN ID is kept (0 only when no valid one is stored). See Defaults.

Response: Loaded default config!

docs.title: #Pullconfig
docs.text:
Get

Prints the whole configuration on one line, for Motor GUI.

Response: the configuration

docs.title: #Info
docs.text:
Action

Prints the hardware version, batch date and firmware version, the control loop's execution time, the CAN ID, the calibration state, the thermistor and the supply voltage, the phase direction, phase order and commutation direction, and the motor parameters (pole pairs, angle offset, R, L, Kt, KV). From firmware 109 also the build, the board ID and the calibration ID, the CAN receive overruns and dropped transmits, the product, the current-sense zeros, the tool id, the watchdog and its fallback, settings block 2, the anti-cogging, and at the end the In force: section (see Status and diagnostics). Not the serial number (SERNUM), the gains (Param) or the errors (Error).

Response: the report

docs.title: #Tone
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument f,mA[,ms], or offEnters position mode

A tone through the motor (see Sound): #Tone 440,250,1000 plays 440 Hz at a loudness of 250 mA for 1000 ms, on the axis parameter 82 picks. mA left out: 200; ms left out: 500; ms 0: until #Tone off. 20 Hz up to below 3125 Hz. It plays only while the driver holds or moves; from idle a calibrated driver first holds the position it is at (#Idle releases it). #Tone alone or #Tone off stops all sound. Added in firmware 109.

Response: Tone 440 Hz, 250 mA, 1000 ms; from idle first Holding the position while it plays (#Idle releases it); Tone: not played (…) when it cannot; Tone off

docs.title: #Par
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: n, or n,value

Any parameter by its number (see Parameters and buffers): alone it lists every parameter, #Par 56 reads one, #Par 56,0 sets it (no spaces); a gain or limit (8-16, 20) takes a decimal, e.g. #Par 9,0.02 sets Kpv. Added in firmware 109.

Response: P<n> = <value>; refused: out of range, read only, not now, or unknown when the driver did not take it; P<n> unknown

docs.title: #Tool
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: 0 to 255

The tool id: what the drive is built into, 0 none, 1 SSG-48, 11-33 MSG (tens = rail 1/2/3 = 100/150/200 mm, units = stepper 1/2/3 = 21.5/40/60 mm), 200-254 your own. The same as parameter 1. Kept by Save. Added in firmware 109.

Response: Tool ID: N, or Invalid tool id (0-255)

docs.title: #WdFb
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int list: time_ms,current_mA,speed_ticks_s,after_action

The watchdog fallback, four numbers at once without spaces, e.g. #WdFb 2000,0,1000,2: how long hold or descend runs, descend's current and speed cap, and what follows (0 legacy, 2 brake, 3 coast). The same as parameters 2 to 5, clamped the same way; fewer than four numbers change nothing. Kept by Save. Added in firmware 109.

Response: Watchdog fallback: … ms, … mA, … ticks/s, then …

docs.title: #Product
docs.text:
ActionArgument nothing, or claim, clear

The product lock: prints this firmware and the board's stamp. claim stamps the board as this product (a repaired board, a motor the stamp rule misjudges), clear removes the stamp; power-cycle after either. Over UART only. Added in firmware 109.

Response: Firmware: STEPFOC; board stamp: …

docs.title: #Param
docs.text:
Get

Prints every gain of every loop.

Response: the gains

docs.title: #Help
docs.text:
Action

Prints a short command reference. Added in firmware 106.

Response: the reference

docs.title: #Error
docs.text:
Get

Prints which errors are active.

Response: No errors! or In error state! followed by one line per active error

docs.title: #Clear
docs.text:
ActionEnters idle mode

Clears the errors and goes to idle. An error whose cause is still present comes straight back; a calibration error is cleared only by calibrating (or #Calibrated 1).

Response: Clear errors

docs.title: #Mode
docs.text:
Get

Prints the control mode. The voltage-torque mode prints Gripper mode; HALL, the angle-offset search, open-loop steps (gosteps), gripper mode and the encoder-table run print nothing.

Response: Idle mode, Position control, Speed control, Current control, PD control, Open loop, Gripper mode, Gripper calib mode

docs.title: #Vbus
docs.text:
Get

Prints the supply voltage.

Response: mV

docs.title: #Vmax
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: voltage in mV

The supply voltage above which a Vbus error is raised, 29000 mV after #Default.

Response: Vmax in mV: N

Response: °C, or Temp Off while the thermistor is disabled

docs.title: #Term

Set/GetArgument int: 0 or 1

Enables the thermistor measurement and the temperature error (off by default).

Response: the setting

docs.title: #Tlim
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: temperature in °C

The temperature at which the temperature error is raised; 75 by default.

docs.title: #Iabc

Response: Ia, Ib in mA

docs.title: #PWM

Prints the PWM duty values.

Response: the duties

docs.title: #LED
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: 0 or 1

Turns the status LED on or off.

Response: the LED state

docs.title: #CANID
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: 0 to 13

The CAN node ID. Use 0 to 13: the firmware accepts 14 and 15, but the bootloader reserves them and a driver on one of those cannot be updated over CAN. Kept over a power cycle after Save, which also writes it into the bootloader's board ID; from firmware 109 Default and a settings reset keep it too.

Response: the ID, or Invalid CAN ID

docs.title: #SERNUM
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: number

The serial number. This firmware does not read it back from the EEPROM at power-up: it reports 1 until set, and Save writes the value in RAM over the stored one.

Response: Serial number is: N

docs.title: #Activate
docs.text:
Action

Sets the activated flag.

Response: Controller activated

docs.title: #Cyc
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: interval in ms (0 = off)

Sends position, speed and Iq on its own every interval: $ <position> <speed> <Iq>; for BetterSerialPlotter.

Response: Cyclic disabled when turned off

docs.title: #Cyca
docs.text:
Set/GetArgument int: interval in ms (0 = off)

Like Cyc, in the Arduino plotter format Position:x,Speed:y,Iq:z.

Response: Cyclic disabled when turned off

docs.title: Getting help
docs.text:
• Questions and discussion: the Source Robotics Discord.
  • A problem with the driver or the firmware: an issue in the firmware repository; see Report a problem for what to include.
  • A mistake on a page of this site: every page ends with a link to edit it and one to report it; see Contributing.
  • Orders and hardware: source-robotics.com.

Before you ask, Troubleshooting goes through the common symptoms, and #Info tells most of what anyone will ask you for.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: This documentation lives in Source-Robotics/STEPFOC-docs. A small fix can be made from the browser: the Edit it on GitHub link at the end of every page opens the page's source, and GitHub turns your change into a pull request. For anything larger, open an issue first.

docs.title: How the site is built
docs.text:
• The pages are Markdown, built with MkDocs and the Material theme; the repository's README.md says how to preview it locally.
  • The site describes one firmware release, named in versions.yml. The command IDs, frame lengths, the UART command list and the defaults in the Reference are read from the firmware's source at that release's tag by tools/sync_firmware.py; do not edit those facts in the pages. The descriptions of the commands are in docs/includes/can_commands.yml and uart_commands.yml.
  • Every push runs a strict build (a broken link fails it) and the tool tests. A push to main publishes the site under its firmware version with mike.

docs.title: House rules
docs.text:
• Facts come from the firmware. When a page and the firmware disagree, the firmware is right; fix the page, or report the firmware.
  • Spell commands exactly as the firmware does, even where the spelling looks wrong.
  • Write for someone who has the driver in front of them and wants to do one thing: say what to do, in order, then why.
  • Three kinds of boxes: a note, a notice (damage) and a danger (injury). Use them for those, not for emphasis.
  • Images: under 2400 px on the long side, with a caption that says what the reader should see.

docs.title: Licence
docs.text: Text and images: CC BY-SA 4.0: copy, adapt and share them, also commercially, if you credit Source Robotics and share your changes under the same licence. Code: the MIT licence, which covers the code examples in the pages and the site's own code. The Source Robotics name, the product names and the logos are not covered by either. By contributing you agree that your contribution is published under these licences.

docs.title: Report a problem
docs.text:
Open an issue in the firmware repository for the driver and its firmware, or in Spectral-BLDC-Python for the Python library. Include:

  1. The output of #Info, #Param and #Error, copied from the terminal. They carry the hardware and firmware version, the motor parameters, the calibration state, the gains and limits, and the errors.
  2. The motor: type, and the #R, #L, #PP you entered.
  3. The supply: voltage, and whether it has a current limit.
  4. What you did and what happened: the commands, in order, and the driver's answers; the calibration log if it is about calibration.
  5. How it is wired: a photo of the board on the motor and of the cables helps more than a description.

For a problem with this documentation, the Report it link at the end of the page opens an issue in the documentation repository with the page already named.
